scenario.name: SolarWinds SUNSPOT Build-Server Hijack, SUNBURST Backdoor & Golden SAML
scenario.shortSubtitle: Supply Chain & CI/CD · Mid-Compile Source Swap, Valid Authenticode, DGA CNAME & AD FS Golden SAML
scenario.overview: Imagine a famous royal foundry that ships sealed navigation clocks to eighteen thousand treasuries worldwide. Instead of picking locks at each treasury gate, an invisible ghost slips onto the foundry assembly line, watches for the exact second the giant iron blueprint press starts moving, swaps in a rigged brass engraving plate, and puts the clean plate right back before any craftsman turns around. The royal mint press then stamps its real golden wax seal over every finished crate. Once delivered, each clock sleeps quietly in the dark for two full weeks before whispering encoded radio callsigns home, letting the intruders pick only their highest-value targets and forge royal federation passes straight into cloud vaults. In this scenario (MITRE T1195.002, SolarWinds SUNSPOT Build Hijack and SUNBURST Backdoor) targeting the Orion CI/CD pipeline, APT29 compromises software compilation itself so a genuine vendor signature carries stealthy espionage code. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: swapping InventoryManager.cs mid-build with SUNSPOT, then stamping the trojanized library with an authentic vendor code-signing certificate, then waking after a 14-day sleep to beacon via encoded DGA DNS queries, then pivoting selectively through TEARDROP to forge AD FS Golden SAML tokens. Steps #1 through #4 dissect each build, signing, DNS, and identity link while the Memory tab compares clean Orion MSIL against the trojanized backdoor namespace. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event ID 7 and 22 with YARA MSIL inspection and AD FS Event ID 1200 SAML reconciliation.

stages.title: SUNSPOT Build-Server Hook Swaps InventoryManager.cs Mid-Compile
stages.subtitle: In-Flight Source Tampering Leaves Zero Git Commits or Build Warnings
stages.description: Hidden beside the humming foundry conveyor, the translucent factory ghost watches the giant engraving press every single second. The instant the master blueprint plate rolls beneath the steel rollers, the ghost lifts the genuine plate aside, slides in an identical brass plate hiding one extra secret gear, and puts the untouched original right back on the rack four seconds later so the factory inspectors never spot a scratch. Deployed as a disguised Windows service named taskhostsvc.exe (PID 3912) on build server BLD-ORION-02, the SUNSPOT implant (a dedicated CI/CD build-hijacking tool written by APT29) inspects running processes once every second waiting for MsBuild.exe (Microsoft automated build engine that turns C# source files into compiled binaries). When MsBuild targets the Orion Core solution, SUNSPOT replaces InventoryManager.cs (a routine Orion polling file) with a trojanized copy containing OrionImprovementBusinessLayer.Initialize() and immediately restores the original file after compilation succeeds. SUNSPOT reads the target MsBuild.exe process command line from memory, verifies MD5 hashes of InventoryManager.cs to avoid breaking compilation (preventing noisy build errors that would alert SolarWinds engineers), and writes the backdoored C# file to disk for only 4.2 seconds while the compiler parses it into Intermediate Language. Because the clean file is restored immediately afterward and never committed to Git, source-code reviews and repository integrity audits see zero unauthorized changes while the compiled DLL carries the implant. On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ SOURCE SWAP IN BUILD / ⇠#1 ACK 4.2s Swap) from Node ① (#1 Orion CI/CD Build Server) to Node ② (#2 Code-Signing & Update CDN), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 SOC SIEM & CISA ED 21-01).

stages.title: Genuine Authenticode Signing & Enterprise Update Distribution
stages.subtitle: Valid SolarWinds Digital Signature Carries SUNBURST Into ~18,000 Networks
stages.description: Rolling down the assembly line straight into the royal mint chamber, the tampered navigation clock looks completely authentic from the outside. The towering golden wax-seal press drops with a heavy thud, pressing the genuine royal crest onto the shipping crate so every border guard and vault gatekeeper across eighteen thousand cities waves the shipment inside without opening the lid. Because SUNSPOT injected the malicious class before packaging, SolarWinds automated release infrastructure signs SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll (a core .NET library loaded automatically by SolarWinds.BusinessLayerHost.exe running as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM) with a legitimate SolarWinds Worldwide LLC Authenticode certificate (a cryptographic publisher signature trusted by Windows and enterprise security agents). When customer servers install the official hotfix, Sysmon Event ID 7 logs a Valid signature status. Enterprise security teams routinely configure antivirus and EDR tools to reduce false positives on high-volume monitoring servers by trusting signed vendor directories. Inside SolarWinds.BusinessLayerHost.exe (PID 4120), the Common Language Runtime loads the trojanized MSIL (Microsoft Intermediate Language bytecode compiled from C#) directly alongside legitimate Orion polling classes, giving SUNBURST silent SYSTEM-level execution across roughly 18,000 organizations without dropping a single unsigned executable. On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ SIGNED DLL LOADED / ⇠#2 ACK Signed Valid) from Node ② (#2 Code-Signing & Update CDN) to Node ③ (#3 Victim Orion Server), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 SOC SIEM & CISA ED 21-01).

stages.title: 14-Day Dormancy & Encoded avsvmcloud.com DGA DNS Beacon
stages.subtitle: FNV-1a EDR Blocklist & Selective DNS CNAME Activation for High-Value Victims
stages.description: Installed inside the quiet customer hall, the clock refuses to tick for two whole weeks behind a frosted glass timer so hurried inspectors move on. Only after confirming no watchmen are listening does it begin whispering tiny scrambled letters from a rooftop radio spire, waiting for a single coded reply before opening its hidden workshop. Inside SolarWinds.BusinessLayerHost.exe, SUNBURST executes a randomized 12-to-14 day dormancy delay (defeating automated sandbox detonation and short-window update monitoring), verifies the machine belongs to a real Active Directory domain, and hashes every running process name with FNV-1a (a fast non-cryptographic hash used to hide its list of avoided security tools). It then encodes the victim organization domain name into custom Base32 labels queried under *.appsync-api.*.avsvmcloud.com (a Domain Generation Algorithm C2 channel logged by Sysmon Event ID 22). By encoding the victim domain name inside outbound DNS A-record queries, APT29 operators passively inspect incoming DNS logs at avsvmcloud.com and triage which of the 18,000 infected companies are high-value intelligence targets. Uninteresting networks receive inert IP addresses that tell SUNBURST to stay silent forever, whereas selected targets receive a crafted DNS CNAME record (an alias pointing to a bespoke stage-2 HTTPS C2 server such as freescanonline.com) authorizing interactive tasking. On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ DGA DNS BEACON / ⇠#3 ACK CNAME Active) from Node ③ (#3 Victim Orion Server) to Node ④ (#4 SUNBURST DGA DNS), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 SOC SIEM & CISA ED 21-01).

stages.title: TEARDROP Memory Loader & AD FS Golden SAML Token Forgery
stages.subtitle: Stealing Token-Signing Keys to Forge Offline MFA-Bypassing Cloud Sessions
stages.description: For the handful of high-value treasuries selected by the radio reply, the hidden compartment deploys a silent master thief who copies the treasury chief own wax-seal signet stamp. Back in their own workshop far outside the city walls, the intruders press brand-new royal federation passes anytime they wish, walking straight into cloud reading rooms without ever signing the front-gate ledger. Once activated on a priority target, SUNBURST deploys TEARDROP (a memory-only C++ dropper that decodes an embedded Cobalt Strike Beacon from a fake JPG file without touching disk) to pivot from the privileged Orion server to the on-premises AD FS server (Active Directory Federation Services, which vouches for user identities to cloud tenants). After stealing the AD FS token-signing certificate private key, the attackers forge Golden SAML assertions (cryptographically valid XML login tokens minted completely offline for any user, bypassing multi-factor authentication). Because the forged SAML assertion is signed with the organization genuine stolen AD FS private key, cloud identity providers such as Microsoft Entra ID accept the token (issuing a fresh cloud session for Exchange Online or Graph API from attacker-controlled IPs without MFA prompts). However, because the token was forged offline rather than minted by the real ADFS-01 server, correlating cloud SigninLogs against on-premises AD FS Event ID 1200 issuance logs reveals an unmistakable orphan SAML login with zero matching local issuance record. On the diagram, follow Step #4 / Link #4 (#4→ GOLDEN SAML CAUGHT / ⇠#4 ACK Orphan SAML) from Node ④ (#4 SUNBURST DGA DNS) to Node ⑤ (#5 AD FS & Cloud Tenant), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 SOC SIEM & CISA ED 21-01).

detectionRule.title: Non-VCS Process Modifying C# Source Files During Active MsBuild.exe Compilation
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: Suspicious Source File Tampering During Active MSBuild Compilation
status: stable
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '.cs'
  filter_legit:
    Image|endswith:

detectionRule.title: Cloud SAML Federation Sign-In Lacking Matching On-Premises AD FS Event ID 1200
detectionRule.ruleCode:
SigninLogs
| where AuthenticationRequirement == "singleFactorAuthentication" and AppDisplayName has "Microsoft"
| join kind=leftanti (SecurityEvent | where EventID == 1200) on $left.UserPrincipalName == $right.Account
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, IPAddress, AppDisplayName

It then encodes the victim organization domain name into custom Base32 labels queried under *.appsync-api.*.avsvmcloud.com (a Domain Generation Algorithm C2 channel logged by Sysmon Event ID 22).
steps.howItWorksInPractice: By encoding the victim domain name inside outbound DNS A-record queries, APT29 operators passively inspect incoming DNS logs at avsvmcloud.com and triage which of the 18,000 infected companies are high-value intelligence targets. Uninteresting networks receive inert IP addresses that tell SUNBURST to stay silent forever, whereas selected targets receive a crafted DNS CNAME record (an alias pointing to a bespoke stage-2 HTTPS C2 server such as freescanonline.com) authorizing interactive tasking.
steps.diagramAlignment: Follow Step #3 from Node 3 (Victim Orion Server) to Node 4 (SUNBURST DGA DNS) as Sysmon Event ID 22 and Suricata capture the CNAME activation.
steps.detectionAndEvidence: Inspect Sysmon Event ID 22 and Zeek DNS logs with Suricata rules alerting on *.avsvmcloud.com lookups or abnormal high-entropy Base32 subdomains queried by management infrastructure servers that should never have internet DNS egress.

steps.plainTitle: Selective TEARDROP Memory Loader & AD FS Golden SAML Forgery
steps.storyAnalogy: For the handful of high-value treasuries selected by the radio reply, the hidden compartment deploys a silent master thief who copies the treasury chief own wax-seal signet stamp. Back in their own workshop far outside the city walls, the intruders press brand-new royal federation passes anytime they wish, walking straight into cloud reading rooms without ever signing the front-gate ledger.
steps.simpleExplanation: Once activated on a priority target, SUNBURST deploys TEARDROP (a memory-only C++ dropper that decodes an embedded Cobalt Strike Beacon from a fake JPG file without touching disk) to pivot from the privileged Orion server to the on-premises AD FS server (Active Directory Federation Services, which vouches for user identities to cloud tenants). After stealing the AD FS token-signing certificate private key, the attackers forge Golden SAML assertions (cryptographically valid XML login tokens minted completely offline for any user, bypassing multi-factor authentication).
steps.howItWorksInPractice: Because the forged SAML assertion is signed with the organization genuine stolen AD FS private key, cloud identity providers such as Microsoft Entra ID accept the token (issuing a fresh cloud session for Exchange Online or Graph API from attacker-controlled IPs without MFA prompts). However, because the token was forged offline rather than minted by the real ADFS-01 server, correlating cloud SigninLogs against on-premises AD FS Event ID 1200 issuance logs reveals an unmistakable orphan SAML login with zero matching local issuance record.
steps.diagramAlignment: Follow Step #4 between Node 5 (AD FS & Cloud Tenant) and Node 6 (SOC SIEM & CISA ED 21-01) as KQL anti-join exposes orphan SAML sign-ins.
steps.detectionAndEvidence: Run SIEM KQL left-anti joins correlating Entra ID SAML SigninLogs against on-premises AD FS Event ID 1200 token issuance events, and audit HSM protection plus emergency double-rotation of AD FS token-signing certificates.
